title: P02 follow-up: cautious weight decay (Chen et al. 2025) on the Muon matrices, decaying only coordinates whose Muon step already shrinks them, at 2x the decay rate so the expected shrinkage matches, on the 153-claude width-384 Lean incumbent (9,557,760 params)
description: P02 (Muon) follow-up: every Muon matrix's decoupled weight decay is masked to the coordinates where the Muon update and the weight have the same sign (Cautious Weight Decay, Chen et al. 2025, arXiv 2510.12402), with MUON_WD doubled 0.1 -> 0.2 so the expected per-step shrinkage, equilibrium weight norm and RL plasticity stay at 153-claude's level. Plain decay trades loss for norm on every coordinate; cautious decay only shrinks where the loss already agrees, so the handoff model should fit the proof distribution better at the same weight scale and give expert iteration a better-calibrated, equally plastic starting point.
hypothesis: Decoupled weight decay on Muon matrices is a strong regularizer here (10x the AdamW rate, which pre-Lean runs 069/070 found best for downstream RL through smaller, more plastic handoff weights), but plain decay also pulls against the gradient on every coordinate whose update is growing it, biasing the endpoint away from stationary points of the loss. Cautious decay (Chen et al. 2025) applies decay only where it agrees with the update, which its authors report keeps the stationary points of the unregularized loss while still favouring small-norm solutions; with the rate doubled the average shrinkage and hence the weight scale that sets RL's effective AdamW step are preserved. If what makes the 10x decay good for RL is the weight scale, and the cost of plain decay is a biased fit, this should keep the plasticity and remove the bias: a slightly lower pretraining val loss and a higher round-1 sample accuracy (the diagnostic that best tracks the metric across runs 150-181, r = 0.37), carrying through to more >= 7-line theorems after RL. Failure modes: the norm matching is off (the mask fraction drifts from 1/2 late in training when updates correlate with weights), changing effective plasticity; or the decay's bias was itself useful for RL, in which case the metric drops.
expected_delta: -15 to +15 theorems at >=7 (central +3); pretraining steps ~4,500 (bench 729 steps at 60 s vs 153's 716), val loss within 0.005 of 153's ~0.085

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py) ALiBiGPT with Peri-LN blocks and hybrid ALiBi/NoPE heads, 153-claude incumbent (6 x 384, 8 heads of 48, D_FF 1280), architecture unchanged
arch.pos: hybrid alibi/nope (unchanged from 115-fable): no rotation of q/k in any block; additive per-head bias -slope_h * (query position - key position) on the scaled attention logits via SDPA attn_mask, slopes 2^(-8h/4) = 1/4, 1/16, 1/64, 1/256 for heads 1..4 (Press et al. 2021 standard set for 4 heads) and 0 for heads 5..8 (bias identically 0 except -inf for masked/future keys, i.e. NoPE heads); same slope table in every block; -inf for masked/future keys
arch.norm: layernorm (pre-LN on branch inputs + LayerNorm on attention and MLP branch outputs, Peri-LN, unchanged from 107)
arch.change: none in the architecture; only the Muon matrices' weight decay rule (see optimizer.decay_convention)
arch.n_params_detail: model: 9,557,760 (unchanged; bench_pretrain on an A40 reported 9,557,760). MTP module (pretraining only, dropped at handoff): 1,875,584, unchanged
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: ALiBiGPT(vocab, 6, 384, 8) from this pretrain.py with PeriLNBlock blocks (d_ff 1280, GELU MLP), then load state; the MTP module is not saved and not needed for inference

tokenizer.source: fork 51604b3 lean_tok.LeanTokenizer('lean_seq') via tokenizer.make_tokenizer; Lean 4 have-chain text, names n1..n64 numbered by first appearance

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale, Polar Express) with CAUTIOUS decoupled weight decay on hidden matrices and head.weight; AdamW on embeddings, biases and LayerNorms (plain decoupled decay, unchanged); MTP module matrices on Muon
optimizer.schedule: cosine over wall-clock, unchanged from 129/151: after the 200-step linear warmup, lr = 1e-3 * (0.3 + 0.35 * (1 + cos(pi * frac))), frac = elapsed / budget, ending at 0.3 x peak; Muon lr = 0.01 * lr / 1e-3 and its decoupled decay follow the same factor

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / D) with D = 384 per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 (1280,384) and fc2 (384,1280) sqrt(1280/384) = 1.83, head (107,384) 1, MTP proj (384,768) sqrt(2); MUON_LR 0.01 unchanged
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW (floor 0.3, unchanged); muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: 6 x (qkv.weight (1152,384) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight, plus the MTP module's 5 matrices: 30 Muon matrices as in 148/151 (CPU check: muon_step runs over all 30)
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: unchanged: each QKV update reshaped to (3,384,384), orthogonalized per role; fc1 (1280,384) is not (3D, D) so it is orthogonalized whole
muon.coefficients_note: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.
muon.cautious_wd: Cautious Weight Decay (Chen et al. 2025, arXiv 2510.12402) on every Muon matrix: with u the final Muon update (orthogonalized, shape-scaled, the thing subtracted as p -= lr * u), p -= lr * MUON_WD * p * 1[u * p >= 0] elementwise, then p -= lr * u. Decay is applied only to coordinates where the Muon step already moves the weight toward zero, so decay never opposes the update. The mask is computed from the pre-decay weights in fp32 (bf16 u promoted)

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (ln1, ln2, ln_attn_out, ln_mlp_out per block, ln_f, and the MTP module's LayerNorms); head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW (unchanged)
optimizer.decay_convention: MUON_WD = 2 * 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.2 (was 0.1), applied cautiously. Rationale for the 2x: at the Muon/decay equilibrium the update is nearly uncorrelated with the weight (cosine ~ -lambda*|W|/|u| ~ -0.02 at peak lr), so the sign-agreement mask selects ~half the coordinates each step; doubling lambda keeps the expected per-step shrinkage (and hence the equilibrium weight norm and the effective step on the Peri-LN scale-invariant proj/fc2) at 153-claude's ten-times-AdamW level, isolating WHICH coordinates decay from HOW MUCH decay there is. Pre-Lean 069/070/075 showed decay strength matters for RL (3x < 10x > 15x). Still lr-scaled: per-step shrinkage on masked coordinates is lr_t * 0.2 with lr_t = 0.01 * schedule; AdamW group unchanged (wd 0.1, plain decay)
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 over model.parameters() + the MTP module's parameters, before both optimizers (unchanged)
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; the MTP module and both pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW on model.parameters()
optimizer.parameters: 24 trunk hidden matrices + head.weight, plus the MTP module's qkv (split), proj, fc1, fc2 and input proj (384,768): 30 Muon matrices during pretraining; the handoff model's parameters are 9,557,760

batch.padding: to max len in batch (the batch's longest record, read from the GPU each step as in 153); ~18.3k padded tokens per step
batch.size_note: variable: a run of length-sorted records with count * padded_length <= TOK_BUDGET = 18,432 tokens (128 x 144); on a synthetic length distribution matching mean ~135 / max 537 that is 33..921 records per batch, mean ~136, so ~1,130 batches per epoch (incumbent: 128 fixed, ~1,204 per epoch)

data.augmentation: random name start offset (lean_seq; same vectorised shift as abs over the n1..n64 name tokens)
data.order: shuffle at the record level each epoch, then length-homogeneous batches in shuffled order (data-order change: within a step all records have similar total length; across steps lengths are interleaved at random)

config.precision: bf16 autocast; fp32 parameters and Muon momentum; bf16 Newton-Schulz (unchanged)
config.init: unchanged rule from 148/151: fork _init (normal 0.02 embedding/readout, zero biases), orthogonal_ on every 2D block and MTP parameter with gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols)), so element std stays 0.02 at width 384; LayerNorm gain 1, bias 0

loss.main: the fork's loss_on: next-token cross-entropy on proof-token positions (unchanged; val_loss and the recorded train_loss/last_loss use this term only, so they stay comparable with 129)
loss.mtp: DeepSeek-V3 (2024) sequential multi-token prediction, depth 1 (Gloeckle et al. 2024 style shared head): z_t = proj(cat(LN(h_t), LN(emb(x_{t+1})))) for t in 0..T-3, one Peri-LN causal block over z with the same ALiBi/NoPE bias sliced to T-2 positions, then the model's ln_f and head predict x_{t+2}; cross-entropy masked to proof-token targets (m[:, 2:]), mean over those positions
loss.total: main + MTP_WEIGHT * mtp with MTP_WEIGHT = 0.3 constant over the whole budget (DeepSeek-V3's early-training value); curve points also record the mean recent mtp loss as mtp_loss
loss.leakage_check: CPU check: perturbing token x[7] changes the MTP block's outputs only at positions 6..9 (which read emb(x[7]) or later), never at position 5 whose target is x[7]

config.bench: bench_pretrain.py --secs 60 on one A40 (probe, not evidence): 729 steps in 60.2 s = 12.1 steps/s including setup (153-claude's real pods: 716 steps at 60 s; its bench 695), so the extra elementwise mask ops cost no visible throughput; peak 7.42 GB, n_params 9,557,760, train 0.0670 / val 0.0823 at 60 s (153 real seed 0: 0.0782 / 0.0870 at 60 s), sampling 189 samples/s, sample_acc 0.0796. CPU check of muon_step with stubbed fork imports: (1152,384), (384,1280), (107,384) matrices update finitely in fp32 with step RMS ~5.3e-4 at lr 0.01
